```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE)
library(data.table)
# R code here is ASCII only (HTML entities for special characters), so the page renders the same in any locale
A <- "docs/assets/grant_figures"
fmt <- function(n) format(n, big.mark=",", trim=TRUE, scientific=FALSE)
fp <- function(x) format(signif(x, 2))
cnt <- fread(file.path(A, "filter_counts.tsv"))[timepoint != "any timepoint"]
fo <- fread(file.path(A, "fdr_overview.tsv"))[tp %in% c("0hr", "1hr", "6hr")]
st <- fread(file.path(A, "gtex_brain_tissues_stats.tsv"))
sc <- function(t) { d <- fread(file.path(A, sprintf("gtex_sqtl_scatter_filter_0hr_Brain_%s.tsv", t))); ct <- cor.test(d$dpsi, d$slope)
  list(n=nrow(d), genes=uniqueN(d$gene), r=unname(ct$estimate), p=ct$p.value) }
cx <- sc("Cortex"); cb <- sc("Cerebellum")
en <- fread(file.path(A, "ctwas_enrichment_filter_reads10nc_stim_joint.tsv")); eu <- en[tp == "0hr"]; es <- en[tp == "stim"]
ex <- fread(file.path(A, "examples.tsv")); ly <- ex[gene == "LY6H"]; my <- ex[gene == "MYT1L"]
g8 <- fread(file.path(A, "genes_pip08.tsv")); j3 <- fread(file.path(A, "joint3_params.tsv"))   # 3-group joint run: genes
# cTWAS with GTEx QTLs: top-3 isoQTL run (esh; Xin, 2026-11-07), h2g bars from the original fit, Venn after post-processing
pie <- fread(file.path(A, "ctwas_h2g_bars_esh.tsv")); pc <- function(t) sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * pie[type == t, prop_heritability])
p1 <- fread(file.path(A, "ctwas_h2g_pie_est.tsv"))   # top 1, for the caveat
vn <- fread(file.path(A, "ctwas_gene_venn_e_esh_pp.tsv")); pps <- fread(file.path(A, "ctwas_pp_summary.tsv"))
fig <- function(f) sprintf("![](assets/grant_figures/%s.png)\n\n[Open as PDF](assets/grant_figures/%s.pdf)\n", f, f)
```

Each panel says what it shows, which results it uses and where the details are. All allele-specific
results are from **read-based isoLASER** (each read's own alignment decides
whether it includes the tested exonic part) and use **isoLASER + filter**:
isoLASER's `cis` label, recomputed on the panel-heterozygous donors with at least
10 reads each, plus |&Delta;PSI| &ge; 0.05. No q-value cutoff.

# Part 1: allele-specific splicing (isoLASER)

## Allele-specific events per timepoint {.tabset}

### Exonic parts and genes

```{r bars_parts, results="asis"}
cat(fig("allelic_effect_counts_filter_exonic_parts"))
```

### Isoforms and genes

```{r bars_iso, results="asis"}
cat(fig("allelic_effect_counts_filter_isoforms"))
```

## {.unlisted .unnumbered}

- **Exonic part:** the unit isoLASER tests, a segment that is exonic in some of a
  gene's transcripts and intronic in others:
  `r paste(fmt(cnt$exonic_parts), collapse=" / ")` at 0 / 1 / 6 hr, in
  `r paste(fmt(cnt$genes), collapse=" / ")` genes.
- **Isoform** (our definition): an annotated transcript that contains an associated
  exonic part (`r paste(fmt(cnt$isoforms), collapse=" / ")`). isoLASER tests parts,
  not transcripts, so this counts isoforms whose usage the allele can shift, not
  isoforms each tested on their own.
- **More events at later timepoints** follow sequencing depth: the number of tested
  associations rises from `r fmt(fo$tested[1])` to `r fmt(fo$tested[2])` and `r fmt(fo$tested[3])`.
  These are discovery counts, not evidence of more allele-specific splicing after
  stimulation.

## Agreement with GTEx brain sQTLs (0 hr) {.tabset}

### Cortex

```{r scatter_cortex, results="asis"}
cat(fig("gtex_sqtl_scatter_filter_0hr_Brain_Cortex"))
```

### Cerebellum

```{r scatter_cerebellum, results="asis"}
cat(fig("gtex_sqtl_scatter_filter_0hr_Brain_Cerebellum"))
```

## {.unlisted .unnumbered}

- **Each point** is one pair: an allele-specific association (SNP &times; exonic part)
  and the GTEx v8 sQTL effect of the same SNP on that event's skipping junction, in
  the same gene. A skipping junction moves opposite to the part's inclusion, so
  agreement is a **negative** correlation.
- **Cortex:** R = `r sprintf("%.2f", cx$r)` (`r cx$n` pairs, `r cx$genes` genes). **Cerebellum:**
  R = `r sprintf("%.2f", cb$r)` (`r cb$n` pairs, `r cb$genes` genes).
- **Across all `r nrow(st)` combinations** (9 brain tissues with full GTEx results, 3
  timepoints), R is negative in `r st[pearson_r < 0, .N]`, from `r sprintf("%.2f", max(st$pearson_r))`
  to `r sprintf("%.2f", min(st$pearson_r))`. The p-values on the plots are nominal, and
  pairs share genes and SNPs.
- Only associations whose exonic part is in an annotated skipping or alternative
  splice-site event, with that junction measured by GTEx, can be paired, so the
  points are a subset of the bar plot's events.

## cTWAS enrichment of allele-specific QTLs in SCZ

```{r enrichment, results="asis"}
cat(fig("ctwas_enrichment_filter_reads10nc_stim_joint"))
```

- **Enrichment:** log2 of the splicing-QTL prior over the SNP prior (cTWAS
  `log_enrichment` / ln 2), &plusmn; 1 SE, in the PGC SCZ GWAS (`ieu-b-5102`).
  Unstimulated `r sprintf("%.1f", eu$log2_enrichment)` &plusmn; `r sprintf("%.1f", eu$log2_se)`
  (p = `r fp(eu$enrichment_pval)`); stimulated `r sprintf("%.1f", es$log2_enrichment)` &plusmn;
  `r sprintf("%.1f", es$log2_se)` (p = `r fp(es$enrichment_pval)`).
- **Design:** one joint cTWAS run with two groups. Unstimulated is 0 hr
  (`r fmt(eu$group_size)` traits); stimulated pools 1 hr and 6 hr
  (`r fmt(es$group_size)` traits, one per exonic part, its QTL from the timepoint with
  the smaller permutation p). One trait per exonic part, with one SNP.

## cTWAS genes (combined_pip &ge; 0.8)

From the joint cTWAS run with **0, 1 and 6 hr as separate groups** (the same
isoLASER + filter weights, `r fmt(sum(j3[group != "SNP", group_size]))` traits): `r nrow(g8)` genes reach
`combined_pip` &ge; 0.8.

```{r genes8}
cell <- function(x) fifelse(is.na(x), "&ndash;", sprintf("%.2f", x))
knitr::kable(g8[, .(gene_name, combined_pip=sprintf("%.2f", combined_pip), `0hr_pip`=cell(pip_0hr), `1hr_pip`=cell(pip_1hr), `6hr_pip`=cell(pip_6hr),
  `QTL SNP`=ukb_id, `&Delta;PSI`=sprintf("%+.3f", dpsi), `Permutation p`=fp(qtl_p), `SCZ GWAS p (SNP)`=fp(gwas_p),
  `Best GWAS p within 250 kb`=fp(nearby_min_p))], escape=FALSE, align="lrrrrlrrrr")
```

- **combined_pip:** over all of the gene's exonic parts and timepoints;
  **0hr_pip, 1hr_pip, 6hr_pip:** from that timepoint's traits only
  ("&ndash;": none in a fine-mapped region).
- **QTL SNP, &Delta;PSI, permutation p:** the gene's trait with the largest PIP. LY6H's
  two top parts tie (same SNP); the example figure below shows the one with the larger
  effect (+0.25).
  **SCZ GWAS p:** of that SNP; **best within 250 kb:** genome-wide significance is
  p < 5e-8.
- NDRG4, SF3B1 and MYT1L sit at genome-wide significant SCZ loci, and LY6H has
  the strongest splicing effect. CNPPD1, PIGF, GOPC, MRPL43 and YWHAE have no
  genome-wide significant SNP within 250 kb. Details: [cTWAS with isoLASER + filter
  QTLs](isolaser_ctwas_scz_filter.html).

## Example gene {.tabset}

### LY6H (6 hr)

```{r ex_ly6h, results="asis"}
cat(fig("isoform_LY6H_6hr"))
```

### MYT1L (6 hr)

```{r ex_myt1l, results="asis"}
cat(fig("isoform_MYT1L_6hr"))
```

## {.unlisted .unnumbered}

Only 6 hr is shown: it is the timepoint that gives both genes their cTWAS PIP.

- **LY6H** (combined_pip `r sprintf("%.2f", ly$combined_pip)`): `r ly$snp` with &Delta;PSI
  `r sprintf("%+.2f", ly$dpsi)`, permutation p &le; 1 &times; 10<sup>-6</sup> (the floor of
  a million permutations), `r ly$n_het` heterozygous donors, `r fmt(ly$reads)` reads. The
  effect has the same sign at 0 and 1 hr. Our suggested highlight.
- **MYT1L** (combined_pip `r sprintf("%.2f", my$combined_pip)`): `r my$snp`, a genome-wide
  significant SCZ SNP, but &Delta;PSI `r sprintf("%+.2f", my$dpsi)`, permutation p
  `r fp(my$perm_p)`, from `r my$n_het` heterozygous donor.
- **Reading the numbers:** beside each isoform, "n (k)" is n reads assigned to that
  transcript and k of them that include the tested part by their own alignment. A
  read can match a skipping isoform everywhere except at the part, so k can be above
  0 there. The bottom row holds reads assigned to transcripts that do not reach the
  part. PSI = the sum of k over the sum of n, which is what the test uses (before
  isoLASER's per-donor depth rescaling).

# Part 2: brain eQTL, sQTL and isoQTL (cTWAS)

cTWAS for SCZ with GTEx v8 Brain Cerebellum QTLs: eQTLs and sQTLs (the M-cTWAS
paper's PredictDB models) and isoQTLs (isoform-expression QTLs from the isoTWAS
models of Bhattacharya et al. 2023). For each isoform we kept the 3 SNPs with the
largest standardised weights (the top-3 run). Details: [cTWAS with GTEx molecular QTLs](ctwas_gtex_isoform_scz.html),
with the post-processing in [its own section](ctwas_gtex_isoform_scz.html#post-processing).

## Share of SCZ heritability

```{r pie, results="asis"}
cat(fig("ctwas_h2g_bars_esh"))
```

Each bar is a QTL type's `prop_heritability` (its share of the SCZ SNP heritability,
h<sup>2</sup><sub>g</sub>) in the eQTL + sQTL + isoQTL (top 3) run: eQTL `r pc("eQTL")`, sQTL
`r pc("sQTL")`, isoQTL `r pc("isoQTL")`, together
`r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * pie[type != "SNP", sum(prop_heritability)])`. The rest is from SNPs not
mediated by these traits. cTWAS gives no standard error for these shares.

**Caveat:** post-processing (next panel) does not re-estimate these shares, so
they come from the fit before it. In that fit, many top-3 isoQTL traits took PIP
at LD-region boundaries that they lose after region merging
(`r pps[run == "esh", genes_pip08_before]` genes at `combined_pip` &ge; 0.8 before,
`r pps[run == "esh", genes_pip08_after]` after). The isoQTL share is therefore
probably inflated. With only the top SNP per isoform it is
`r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * p1[type == "isoQTL", prop_heritability])`.

## Genes found with eQTLs alone and with all three

```{r venn, results="asis"}
cat(fig("ctwas_gene_venn_e_esh_pp"))
```

Genes with `combined_pip` &ge; 0.8 in an eQTL-only run and in the eQTL + sQTL +
isoQTL (top 3) run (same settings), both after post-processing (region merging
and the LD-mismatch check, as in the M-cTWAS paper). The joint run finds
`r vn[region == "esh only", .N]` genes the eQTL-only run misses
(`r vn[region == "esh only" & top_type_esh == "isoQTL", .N]` via isoQTLs,
`r vn[region == "esh only" & top_type_esh == "sQTL", .N]` via sQTLs; listed in the figure, by `combined_pip`)
and misses `r vn[region == "e only", .N]`. "Via" is the QTL type with the largest PIP for that gene.
Of the `r vn[region == "e only", .N]` missed, `r vn[region == "e only" & combined_pip_esh >= 0.5, .N]` are just below the cutoff in the
joint run (`r vn[region == "e only" & combined_pip_esh >= 0.5][order(-combined_pip_esh), paste(sprintf("%s %.3f", gene_name, combined_pip_esh), collapse=", ")]`)
and `r vn[region == "e only" & combined_pip_esh < 0.5, .N]` drop further
(`r vn[region == "e only" & combined_pip_esh < 0.5][order(-combined_pip_esh), paste(sprintf("%s %.2f", gene_name, combined_pip_esh), collapse=", ")]`).
